concurrencyAndOwnerReview: No cyclic wait established: pause captures pre-leave task handles; a new reload captures previous task handles and the already-created prior pause. Prior load does not depend on this later pause. Multiple quick leave/reentry chains remain ordered from older tasks/pause to newer reloads.

perform can synchronously request reload while inside controlTask; reload queues a new task waiting the old control, but perform does not await that new load. Therefore the observed self-control dependency does not form a wait cycle.

Publication checks after asynchronous boundaries require current source UUID, visible page, matching load token and noncancelled task before categories, section rows, control values/names or toast. Section queue remains same-owner and stale section ID is rejected. Clear of runningQuickActionID releases a completed control; reentry load waits prior controls before it can create new ones.

Page pause owns a BackgroundTaskHold released in defer. It does not treat Task.cancel as terminal completion, and does not cancel its own save merely because the page left. Existing executor/service termination and source-lock semantics remain authoritative; source inspection cannot establish actual native shutdown latency.

Current source is resolved by UUID after drain. Same-content comparison ignores only response timing and the existing hasSameContent sync clock; rule/settings edits or deletion reject before save. Same service originalSignature/revision checks and actual needSave acknowledgment remain in place. This is a bounded observation, not a new global atomic edit lock.

All quick-action helper entries forward the same injected fetcher. Existing .shared default is retained only for old callers; no internal .shared override remains. Same source open/evaluate/cache owners persist. Removing primeDiscoverCookies only removes the already empty implementation, not a real Cookie operation.
